gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Marantz MODEL 30 (US$3,500 at Abt on 2026-11-14) lists a 75 dB MC phono signal-to-noise ratio, while the Luxman L-505Z (US launch MSRP US$5,995) lists 70 dB (IHF-A). So the cheaper amp has the better moving-coil noise spec on paper.
standout_why: I could not read the cited What Hi-Fi best-buys page (only a 129-character shell came back) or the Stereophile Recommended Components page (403), so I can't confirm those pages lack this. ChatGPT's own answer ranks the amps by sound adjectives ('Excellent MM/MC', 'Good MM') and gives no phono noise figures. The cited Luxman product page lists only the Luxman's specs, with no comparison to the Marantz. The Rhythm Audio/Darko piece is a listening review. ChatGPT's Luxman price of US$6,995 is US$1,000 above Luxman America's published MSRP of US$5,995, and its Musical Fidelity A1 price of US$1,999 is US$300 above the US$1,699 that hi-fi+ printed.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's choice of the Marantz MODEL 30 for moving-coil owners: on the makers' published specs it has the lower-noise MC stage and costs about US$2,500 less than the Luxman. Caveat: the Abt listing gives no weighting for its figures, so the 5 dB gap may come partly from different measurement methods. The Rega Elex Mk4 is out for MC owners because Rega lists a moving-magnet phono stage only. The Musical Fidelity A1 is the cheapest MM/MC option, but it makes 25 W into 8 Ω and ran at about 60 °C in hi-fi+'s test. The Luxman's case rests on 150 W into 4 Ω and its build, not on phono noise.
